questions.question: A cyclic process on a $P$-$V$ diagram consists of: A→B (isobaric expansion at $P = 3\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ from $V = 1\ \mathrm{L}$ to $V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$), B→C (isochoric cooling at $V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$), C→A (isobaric compression at $P = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ from $V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$ to $V = 1\ \mathrm{L}$). Find the net work done per cycle.
questions.answer:
Work is only done in the isobaric steps:

$W_{AB} = P_{AB}(V_B - V_A) = 3\times10^5 \times (4-1)\times10^{-3} = 900\ \mathrm{J}$

$W_{BC} = 0$ (isochoric)

$W_{CA} = P_{CA}(V_A - V_C) = 1\times10^5 \times (1-4)\times10^{-3} = -300\ \mathrm{J}$

$W_{\text{net}} = 900 + 0 + (-300) = 600\ \mathrm{J}$

This equals the area of the rectangle: $(P_{AB} - P_{CA})(V_B - V_A) = (3-1)\times10^5 \times 3\times10^{-3} = 600\ \mathrm{J}$ ✓

questions.question: For the cycle in the previous problem ($W_{\text{net}} = 600\ \mathrm{J}$), the monatomic ideal gas has state A: $P = 3\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V = 1\ \mathrm{L}$; state B: $P = 3\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$; state C: $P = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$. Find $n$ and the heat absorbed in the hot step A→B.
questions.answer:
At state A: $n = \dfrac{P_A V_A}{RT_A}$. Need $T_A$.

Let $T_A$: $T_A = \dfrac{P_A V_A}{nR}$ (circular). Instead, find $n$ using the constraint:

At state C: $T_C = \dfrac{P_C V_C}{nR} = \dfrac{1\times10^5 \times 4\times10^{-3}}{nR} = \dfrac{400}{nR}$

At state A: $T_A = \dfrac{3\times10^5 \times 1\times10^{-3}}{nR} = \dfrac{300}{nR}$

Notice $T_A = T_C = \dfrac{300}{nR}$ (both give the same value: $P_A V_A = P_C V_C = 300\ \mathrm{J}$!)

$n = \dfrac{P_A V_A}{RT_A}$. Take $T_A = 361\ \mathrm{K}$ (if $n=0.1\ \mathrm{mol}$): $T_A = 300/(0.1 \times 8.31) = 361\ \mathrm{K}$

With $n = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}$: $T_B = \dfrac{3\times10^5 \times 4\times10^{-3}}{0.1 \times 8.31} = \dfrac{1200}{0.831} = 1444\ \mathrm{K}$

$Q_{AB} = nC_P\Delta T_{AB} = 0.1 \times \frac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times (1444 - 361) = 0.1 \times 20.775 \times 1083 = 2249\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.question: A Carnot cycle runs between $T_H = 600\ \mathrm{K}$ and $T_C = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. The gas absorbs $Q_H = 1200\ \mathrm{J}$ from the hot reservoir. Find: (a) the efficiency, (b) net work, (c) heat rejected to the cold reservoir.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Carnot efficiency:

$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \dfrac{300}{600} = 0.5 = 50\%$

**(b)** $W = \eta Q_H = 0.5 \times 1200 = 600\ \mathrm{J}$

**(c)** $Q_C = Q_H - W = 1200 - 600 = 600\ \mathrm{J}$ (rejected to cold reservoir)

questions.question: A cycle on a $P$-$V$ diagram consists of an isothermal expansion from A to B, followed by an adiabatic expansion from B to C, then an isochoric process from C back to A. Describe what happens to the gas temperature at each step and whether heat flows in or out.
questions.answer:
**A→B (isothermal expansion):** $T = $ const. Gas expands at constant temperature by absorbing heat from a reservoir: $Q_{AB} > 0$ (heat flows in). $\Delta U = 0$.

**B→C (adiabatic expansion):** $Q = 0$ (no heat flow). Gas expands, does work on surroundings, cools: temperature decreases. $\Delta U < 0$.

**C→A (isochoric):** $V = $ const, $W = 0$. Temperature must return to $T_A$ (since we're back to state A). Since $T_C < T_A$, heat flows **into** the gas to raise its temperature: $Q_{CA} > 0$. $\Delta U = Q_{CA} > 0$.

Net: $\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = 0$ (complete cycle). $W_{\text{net}} = Q_{\text{net}}$.

questions.question: A monatomic ideal gas undergoes a triangular cycle on a $P$-$V$ diagram with vertices at: A$(1\times10^5, 1\times10^{-3})$, B$(3\times10^5, 1\times10^{-3})$, C$(1\times10^5, 3\times10^{-3})$ (in Pa and m³). Find the net work done by the gas.
questions.answer:
The cycle forms a right triangle in the $P$-$V$ plane.

Net work = area of triangle:

$W_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$

Base (along $V$-axis from A to C at $P = 1\times10^5$): $\Delta V = 3\times10^{-3} - 1\times10^{-3} = 2\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

Height (along $P$-axis from A to B at $V = 1\times10^{-3}$): $\Delta P = 3\times10^5 - 1\times10^5 = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

$W_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\times10^{-3} \times 2\times10^5 = 200\ \mathrm{J}$

(Positive if traversed counterclockwise — check the orientation based on the given path.)

questions.question: In a complete thermodynamic cycle, the gas performs net work $W_{\text{net}} = 500\ \mathrm{J}$. The cycle has two steps where heat is absorbed ($Q_1 = 800\ \mathrm{J}$, $Q_2 = 400\ \mathrm{J}$) and one step where heat is released. Find $Q_3$ (heat released).
questions.answer:
For a complete cycle: $\Delta U = 0$, so $Q_{\text{net}} = W_{\text{net}}$

$Q_1 + Q_2 + Q_3 = W_{\text{net}}$

$800 + 400 + Q_3 = 500$

$Q_3 = 500 - 1200 = -700\ \mathrm{J}$

The gas releases $700\ \mathrm{J}$ in step 3.

questions.question: Explain the sign convention for net work done in a cyclic process on a $P$-$V$ diagram: when is the net work positive (clockwise) vs. negative (counterclockwise)?
questions.answer:
Work done by the gas $= \int P\,dV$ = area under the $P$-$V$ curve.

**Clockwise cycle:** The upper path (expansion) has higher pressure than the lower path (compression). So the expansion step does more positive work than the compression step does negative work.

$W_{\text{net}} = \oint P\,dV > 0$ ✓ (engine: gas does net work on surroundings)

**Counterclockwise cycle:** The compression path has higher pressure — more work is done **on** the gas than the gas does on surroundings.

$W_{\text{net}} = \oint P\,dV < 0$ (refrigerator/pump: net work done on gas)

**Magnitude:** In both cases $|W_{\text{net}}| = $ area enclosed by the cycle.

questions.question: A heat engine operates on a rectangular cycle (on a $P$-$V$ diagram) with $P_H = 4\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $P_L = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V_1 = 2\ \mathrm{L}$, $V_2 = 6\ \mathrm{L}$. Find: (a) net work per cycle, (b) the efficiency if the heat input is $Q_H = 3000\ \mathrm{J}$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Net work = area of rectangle:

$W = (P_H - P_L)(V_2 - V_1) = (4-1)\times10^5 \times (6-2)\times10^{-3}$

$= 3\times10^5 \times 4\times10^{-3} = 1200\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** $\eta = \dfrac{W}{Q_H} = \dfrac{1200}{3000} = 0.4 = 40\%$

questions.question: A gas undergoes a cycle: A→B (isobaric at $P = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ from $V = 1\ \mathrm{L}$ to $4\ \mathrm{L}$), B→C (isochoric), C→A (isothermal). Find: (a) the pressure at C, (b) the net work (approximate, using only the exact work from A→B and B→C).
questions.answer:
**(a)** For the isothermal path C→A: $T_C = T_A$.

At A: $P_A = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V_A = 1\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

At C: $V_C = V_B = 4\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$ (from the isochoric B→C)

Isothermal C→A: $P_C V_C = P_A V_A \Rightarrow P_C = \dfrac{P_A V_A}{V_C} = \dfrac{2\times10^5 \times 1}{4} = 0.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

**(b)** $W_{AB} = 2\times10^5 \times 3\times10^{-3} = 600\ \mathrm{J}$

$W_{BC} = 0$ (isochoric)

$W_{CA} = nRT\ln(V_A/V_C) = P_A V_A \ln(1/4) = 200 \times (-1.386) \approx -277\ \mathrm{J}$ (compression)

$W_{\text{net}} \approx 600 + 0 - 277 = 323\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.question: On a $P$-$V$ diagram, two different cycles have the same enclosed area but one is clockwise and the other is counterclockwise. Describe what each cycle represents physically and what happens to $Q_{\text{net}}$ in each case.
questions.answer:
Both cycles have $|W_{\text{net}}|$ equal to the same enclosed area.

**Clockwise cycle (heat engine):**
- $W_{\text{net}} > 0$: gas does positive net work on surroundings
- $Q_{\text{net}} = W_{\text{net}} > 0$: gas absorbs net heat from reservoirs
- Converts heat to work (engine)

**Counterclockwise cycle (refrigerator/heat pump):**
- $W_{\text{net}} < 0$: net work done **on** the gas
- $Q_{\text{net}} = W_{\text{net}} < 0$: gas rejects net heat to surroundings
- Uses work to move heat from cold to hot (refrigerator)

In both cases $\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = 0$ since the state returns to its initial value.
